target: route "precondition": Preconditioning the survival operator by a change of measure

findings.defect: FALSE AS STATED. The claim that Lambda(WD(e,j,m)) = 1/(2u) with sum_{k=1}^{e} u^k = 1/(2u), 'independent of j and m', holds only when e >= j. The proof step 'the remaining three profiles replace one or both a-branches by b-branches, ... and are therefore faster' is wrong: the b-branch profile satisfies the SAME equation with e replaced by j (eigenvector: x(w_q)=0, x(c_{i,j-1})=u, x(c_{i,q})=u(1+x(c_{i,q+1})), x(b_i)=sum_{k=1}^{j}u^k = rho = 1/(2u)). The correct statement is Lambda(WD(e,j,m)) = 1/(2u) with sum_{k=1}^{max(e,j)} u^k = 1/(2u), i.e. 1-Lambda = (1/3)2^{-max(e,j)}(1+o(1)). The route's verification is exactly the failure mode rule 3 warns about: it varied e over 2..8 while FREEZING j=2, and then asserted independence of j.
findings.evidence: Exact bisection of the certificate programme (independent code, M-matrix criterion on I-M_pi/lam, all 2^{|C|} profiles) over 49 triples e=1..7, j=2..8, m=j+3: 24 of them contradict the route's formula and all 49 match f(max(e,j)) to 1e-9. Examples: Lambda(WD(2,7,11)) = 0.997342154365, route formula gives 0.884646177119 (= f(2)); the measured value is f(7). Lambda(WD(1,8,11)) = 0.99868295943 = f(8) against route's f(1) = 0.70710678119. Lambda(WD(4,8,12)) = 0.998682959429 = f(8) against route's f(4) = 0.976750818608. Zero mismatches against f(max(e,j)) over all 49.

findings.defect: UNATTRIBUTED STANDARD MATHEMATICS. The theorem 'for a rectangular family {M_pi} of nonnegative matrices with Sx = max_pi M_pi x, lambda* = lim ||S^k 1||^{1/k} = max_pi rho(M_pi), certified by policy iteration' is published prior art, and the route attributes nothing. It is the joint-spectral-radius identity for sets of nonnegative matrices with independent row uncertainty (Blondel-Nesterov, SIAM J. Matrix Anal. Appl. 31 (2009)), equivalently the optimality of stationary policies for the maximal growth rate in nonnegative dynamic programming (Rothblum/Zijm/Sladky lineage; 's-rectangularity implies stationary optimality' in robust MDPs), with clause (ii) being textbook policy iteration for the scaled positive MDP. This is the ninth candidate for the project's prior-art list. rem:prec-attribution attributes Meyer and Jacobi but is silent on the route's own headline theorem. thm:prec-invariance (diagonal conjugation preserves the spectral radius) is likewise a classical one-liner presented as a theorem; lem:prec-monomial IS correctly labelled classical, so the omission is inconsistent rather than systematic.
findings.evidence: The proof given is verbatim the standard argument (Collatz-Wielandt for (i); greedy improvement with (I-A_pi)^{-1} = sum A_pi^k and strict monotone increase for (ii); Fekete on the submultiplicative ||S^k 1|| for (iii)). Nothing in the statement or proof uses any SSG-specific structure -- the route itself says so ('any rectangular family of nonnegative matrices'). frontier.tex contains no such result (grep 'spectral radius|Collatz|Perron' returns only lem:denominator-sharp, thm:impedance and prop:cw), so it is new to the paper but not to the literature.

findings.defect: FALSE AS STATED. 'h = val ... lambda_1 >= 1 on every game with a controlled vertex, and lambda_1 = 1 if that vertex is Max' is false. The proof step '(S val)(v) = max_i val(v^{(i)})' forgets that S reads BOTH sinks as 0 (def:survival), so a controlled vertex with a t_1 successor has (S val)(v) < val(v). The correct hypothesis is that some controlled vertex has both successors off the sinks. (Separately, h = val is not a legal gauge at all whenever val vanishes somewhere, which is generic.)
findings.evidence: Exact counterexample, verified: the 4-vertex stopping SSG v in Vmax with v -> (t_1, w), w in Vavg with w -> (t_0, t_1). It is stopping, val = (1, 1/2) is strictly positive so val IS a legal gauge, and lambda_1(val) = max((S val)(v)/val(v), (S val)(w)/val(w)) = max((1/2)/1, 0/(1/2)) = 1/2 < 1. The one-vertex game v -> (t_1, t_0) gives lambda_1(val) = 0.

findings.defect: The stated iff is wrong in the reverse direction. 'G^h is again an SSG iff h is constant on each connected component of the graph joining every AVERAGE vertex to its two successors' constrains only Vavg, but def:prec-gauge defines P^h(u,v) := P(u,v) h(v)/h(u) on all of V, so at a controlled vertex P^h(v, v^{(i)}) = h(v^{(i)})/h(v), which must also be 1 for G^h to be a game rather than a killed kernel. The correct condition is h constant on the components of the graph joining EVERY non-sink to its successors -- which on a stopping game forces h constant. The parenthetical gloss 'every average vertex a fair coin' half-admits this; the surrounding text (and rem:prec-format, which draws a real conclusion from (d)) reads it as the SSG format condition.
findings.evidence: Direct from def:prec-gauge as written: for v in Vmax with successors v^(0), v^(1), the transformed kernel row is (h(v^(0))/h(v), h(v^(1))/h(v)), which is a choice of two probability-1 moves only if h(v) = h(v^(0)) = h(v^(1)).

findings.defect: The stated fixed-point precision p := Theta(a + log_2 (1/(1-Lambdahat))) is insufficient. The width recursion in the proof is w_{k+1} <= Shat w_k + 2^{1-p} 1, whose accumulated floor against a certificate (lambdahat, xhat) is 2^{1-p} kappahat/(1-lambdahat) -- the proof writes exactly this -- so p must also absorb log_2 kappahat, which the route's own cor:prec-characterisation proof bounds only by O(n log n + n log(1/(1-lambda))). Repair: p = Theta(a + log_2 kappahat + log_2(1/(1-Lambdahat))), still polynomial, so the theorem survives; the statement as written does not.
findings.evidence: The route's own proof line: '||u_k - l_k||_inf <= lambdahat^k kappahat + 2^{1-p} kappahat/(1-lambdahat), which is below 4^{-a} for the stated p and k' -- the second term contains kappahat, which the stated p does not control. The implementation (t_algo.py) uses p = 4a+40, which happens to suffice on every instance measured because kappahat is O(1) there, so the tests cannot detect this.

findings.defect: The one-line proof is incomplete. From 'G' has val_{G'} = val_G off v' one does not get the comparison val_G(v^{(0)}) vs val_G(v^{(1)}) for free: those numbers require SOLVING G', which is again an SSG. The repair is to iterate the hypothesised elimination |C| times down to a player-free game (one linear solve) and back-substitute; that works, but it is not what is written. Separately, the result is an immediate corollary of thm:decide-one-bit -- the route says so, so this is labelling-honest, but it carries no independent content.
findings.evidence: prop:prec-onectrl proof text: 'the outputs of the algorithm therefore name an optimal successor at v'. The output is a game, not a value vector.

findings.defect: OVERCLAIM in the reported headline: 'no Doob/gauge h-transform -- indeed no order-preserving change of variables -- can change it'. What is proved is strictly less: lem:prec-monomial covers (a) LINEAR changes of variable that are monotone with monotone inverse, and (b) SEPARABLE coordinatewise ones, and for (b) only the local linearisation at val, i.e. the local rate of value iteration, not the certificate rate. General order-isomorphisms of R^{V'} (e.g. triangular maps) are untouched. The LaTeX itself is careful ('within linear changes of variable, diagonal is all there is'); the reported headline is not.
findings.evidence: lem:prec-monomial statement and proof: the argument is the classical cone-automorphism fact for A >= 0 with A^{-1} >= 0, plus 'the last clause is the chain rule' for separable Phi.

findings.defect: This is a barrier that covers NONE of M1, M2, M2T, M3, M4, M5, M6 or def:bsi. It bounds only block-Jacobi aggregation, a method the route itself introduces, on LC(k,e) -- a family on which val(v_i) = 1/2 is attained by the fast branch f and every controlled vertex is decided at round 1 by any sound rule. Per the round's own standard, a barrier covering none of the mechanisms is nearly worthless and must be labelled as such; the route labels it only as 'pricing aggregation'. Its mathematical content (r' >= k/b around the cycle, char. poly lambda^{|C|} - q^k lambda^{|C|-r'}) is correct.
findings.evidence: LC(k,e) verified stopping, N = ke+k+3, out-degree two, fair coins, val(v_1) = 1/2 for (k,e) in {(4,3),(5,3),(4,5),(6,3),(4,6),(6,6),(8,6)}; Lambdahat(LC(k,e)) = 1-2^{-e} exactly (0.875, 0.875, 0.96875, 0.875, 0.984375, 0.984375, 0.984375), independent of k, matching the b=1 case of the proposition.

findings.defect: Substantively a restatement of prop:bracket(d) in operator clothing: both say 'a poly-time algorithm producing the certificate object iff SSG-Value in P', and both prove the forward direction by the same 'the answer is its own witness' move (F := the constant map val; there, (w*,w*)). It is honestly labelled target-equivalent, so it is not a circularity defect, but it adds no new equivalence to the seven already proved. Its proof also performs an unjustified rounding step: the hypothesis bounds ||F^k(1)-F^k(0)|| for the EXACT iterates, and no Lipschitz property of F is assumed, so accumulated outward rounding is uncontrolled. The rounding is in fact unnecessary -- 'evaluable in time p(|G|)' already caps the output bit size at p(|G|), so the exact iterates stay polynomial.
findings.evidence: prop:bracket(d) at frontier.tex:5099; thm:prec-target proof at precondition.tex:748-756.

findings.defect: The strictness of contracted-over-escape is witnessed by exactly one construction shape, and it is a dominated decoration: in Y_D (and in the route's minimal loop2) the branch responsible for 1-Lambda = 2^{-Theta(N)} is (a) provably never optimal and (b) annihilated outright by the very row normalisation that defines Lambdahat (Rhat(M_D, A_1; .) = 0). So the class is genuinely strictly larger and genuinely escapes all five bounds, but no member is exhibited whose gain comes from anything other than a self-return that the normalisation deletes. The route does not say this. Also 'contains every player-free game' is vacuous puffery: C empty games are already thm:player-free / thm:kacyclic.
findings.evidence: Verified independently for D=3..8: Y_D is stopping, N=3D+2, a=2D, |Vmax|=D-1, |Vmin|=1, ALL non-sinks reachable from s_D, one SCC of size 3D carrying all three colours, val = val(Z_D) with val(s_D)=1/(2^D-1), d(Y_D)=D (recomputed from def:escape/lem:descent; d(Z_D)=D reproduced, confirming frontier.tex), H(Y_D) one component of size D-1, 1-Lambda(Y_D) = 0.0503, 0.0233, 0.0111, 0.00540, 0.00266 (halving), Lambdahat(Y_D) = 1/2 exactly. Rhat(M_D, action A_1; .) = 0 because the first passage returns to M_D w.p. 1-2^{-D} and dies otherwise.

findings.defect: The claim 'what is specific here is (i) -- that the row normalisation commutes with BOTH max and min, so it is legitimate on a game and not only on a chain' is probably itself standard. Per-action self-loop elimination (divide an action's remaining outgoing mass by 1-p_self) is routine in probabilistic model checking for MDPs and stochastic games, precisely because it is applied per action and therefore commutes with max and with min; combining it with elimination of the purely probabilistic states and then interval iteration is a known pipeline. The mathematics is correct; the novelty claim is the part to check. Also worth noting: the harmonic normal form itself is already in frontier.tex (prop:auso-seven prints one), which the route does mention only via item (v4).
findings.evidence: thm:prec-contract(i)'s pivot is the elementary identity t = max_i(alpha_i t + g_i) iff t = max_i g_i/(1-alpha_i) for alpha_i in [0,1), and dually for min; frontier.tex:2977 already displays a harmonic normal form.

findings.defect: The route reports Y_D only as a class-membership separation ('compared as bounds'). It is more than that: the contracted algorithm beats plain two-sided value iteration EXPONENTIALLY on Y_D as an algorithm, not merely as a bound. This is the strongest single item in the route and it is not stated anywhere in the LaTeX or the JSON.
findings.evidence: Exact rational two-sided iteration of T from (0,1) with sink payoffs carried, rounds until width < 4^{-a}: 40, 106, 270, 667, 1594 for D=3..7 (ratio ~2.4 per increment, 2^{Theta(N)}); the contracted algorithm on the same instances: 13, 17, 21, 25, 29 (= 4D+1). Both returned val exactly.

verdict:
IS IT NEW? Yes relative to frontier.tex, mostly not relative to the literature. Nothing here restates thm:ladder, thm:short-path, lem:cut, lem:duality or thm:seed-dichotomy. But the route's headline theorem thm:prec-rate is published mathematics with no attribution (Blondel-Nesterov's rectangular/independent-row-uncertainty JSR identity; stationary optimality for the maximal growth rate in nonnegative dynamic programming) -- a ninth entry for the project's rediscovery list. thm:prec-invariance is a one-line diagonal-conjugation triviality dressed as a theorem. lem:prec-monomial, Meyer's stochastic complement and Jacobi preconditioning ARE labelled; the claim that "the normalisation commutes with both max and min" is specific is itself likely standard (per-action self-loop elimination in probabilistic model checking). thm:prec-target is prop:bracket(d) in new clothing; prop:prec-onectrl is a stated corollary of thm:decide-one-bit. Genuinely new to the paper: cor:prec-characterisation, thm:prec-contract-class, prop:prec-YD, prop:prec-wedge.

CIRCULAR OR VACUOUS? No circularity. The contracted algorithm assumes no oracle: it computes the first-passage law by one factorisation. The two target-equivalent statements (prop:prec-onectrl, thm:prec-target) are explicitly labelled as such, which is the right behaviour. prop:prec-block is a barrier covering NONE of M1, M2, M2T, M3, M4, M5, M6 or def:bsi -- it bounds only the route's own aggregation method, on an instance every mechanism decides at round 1 -- and must be labelled nearly worthless. The polynomial class IS nonempty and outside all five: I rebuilt Y_D from the LaTeX statement and independently confirmed, on the subgame reachable from s_D (all 3D non-sinks reachable), stopping, N=3D+2, a=2D, one SCC of size 3D with all three colours, |Vmax|=D-1, H(Y_D) one component of size D-1, d(Y_D)=D, 1-Lambda = Theta(2^{-D}), Lambdahat = 1/2, decided in 4D+1 rounds. Y_D and LC(k,e) are legitimate families (build(D)/build(k,e), fair coins, out-degree two, stopping, growth laws measured at >= 5 sizes).

IS THE VERIFICATION HONEST? Mostly yes, and unusually so: the certificate/policy-iteration cross-checks and the harmonic-normal-form checks are cross-validated against brute force, and I reproduced them independently on 400 freshly generated stopping games (|C| = 0..7, n = 3..14) with zero violations of thm:prec-contract(i)-(iii). One failure, and it is the exact failure mode rule 3 names: prop:prec-Gm(b) asserts Lambda(WD(e,j,m)) is independent of j, and was verified only at j=2. Varying j refutes it on 24 of 49 parameter triples; the truth is f(max(e,j)). The route's random sampling is used only where it is legitimate (checking identities, not hunting hard instances) and the hypothesis is genuinely satisfied by the sampled games.

THE REAL REMAINING GAP, stated more precisely than the route states it. The route asks whether the contracted class contains a stall; the harder truth is that it produces no evidence the class is any closer to the frontier than the escape class it enlarges: every member it exhibits outside the escape class (Y_D, loop2, WD(e,2,m)) is decided by the Z-seeded own-successor slack test in O(N) rounds, its own prop:prec-wedge shows that on the ONLY family known to defeat that test the contracted rate 1-Lambdahat = 2^{1-j} IS the silence rate, and every witness of strictness is a branch that is never optimal and that the row normalisation deletes. So the missing statement is: EITHER exhibit a stopping SSG in which the first-passage chain on C with self-returns removed escapes at rate at least 1/poly(N) while some Z-seeded own-successor slack bound at a value-distinguishing controlled vertex stays non-negative for superpolynomially many rounds, OR prove that log_2(1/Lambdahat(G)) times the silence round count is polynomially bounded on every stopping SSG -- which would close the route by showing the contracted class provably cannot reach the frontier, the analogue of rem:escape-class's fourth clause.

BETTER OR WORSE? BETTER, after excisions and two repairs. INTEGRATE: cor:prec-characterisation (it gives the paper an intrinsic spectral characterisation of its own escape class, answering a question the paper poses about itself), thm:prec-invariance + lem:prec-monomial (short, and they retire the change-of-measure idea unconditionally), thm:prec-rate WITH attribution, prop:prec-Gm(a) (correct, and Lambda(Z_D) = 2^{-1/2} confirms prop:escape-family's parenthetical), and the whole contracted block def:prec-contract + lem:prec-wellposed + thm:prec-contract + thm:prec-contract-class + prop:prec-YD + prop:prec-wedge -- this is a sixth polynomial class, disjoint from the five, and I verified it beats plain value iteration EXPONENTIALLY on Y_D as an algorithm (40, 106, 270, 667, 1594 rounds against 13, 17, 21, 25, 29), a fact the route never states and which should go in. REPAIR FIRST: prop:prec-Gm(b) (replace e by max(e,j) or add the hypothesis e >= j) and rem:prec-sharp (its "exactly twice the truth" comparison with rem:escape-class holds only for j <= e); fix rem:prec-candidates(ii), lem:prec-dictionary(d), and the precision p in thm:prec-contract-class. DO NOT INTEGRATE as results: thm:prec-target (demote to one sentence citing prop:bracket(d)), prop:prec-onectrl (one sentence citing thm:decide-one-bit), prop:prec-block (demote to a remark, explicitly labelled as covering none of M1-M6 or def:bsi). Net: the paper gains one real polynomial class with a verified separating family and one clean unconditional negative; it would lose credibility if prop:prec-Gm(b) went in as written.
